newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast spot power steady despite flat load.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast spot power steady despite flat load.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. held steady Wednesday against Tuesday's levels despite flat power demand due to a cool weather system covering much of the region, market sources said.
"Load is flat. Temperatures are not cool enough for much heating demand either," said a regional utility trader.

The bearish effect of low weather-related demand was mitigated by continued congestion at various key interfaces with neighboring power pools, which in turn, prevented cheaper priced electricity to become available in the Northeast bulk power market, traders said.
In the New York Power Pool (NYPP), non-firm electricity for peak load hours on Thursday was assessed at $19.00-$20.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), compared with Tuesday's quote near $19.00.
Next-day power in eastern NYPP was valued at $22.00-$23.00, versus Tuesday's assessment in the $22.00 area.
Off-peak NYPP electricity for Thursday was discussed near $15.00.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity prices for Thursday was pegged at $28.00-$30.00 at the Northeast Utilities' territory border, unchanged from Tuesday's range.
A number of New England utilities expressed buying interests for next-day power down in the $25.00-$26.00 range, according to traders.
